Main.sentence: The Mexico City policy , sometimes referred to by its critics as the global gag rule ,  is a ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ government policy blocking ___E:U.S. federal funding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administration_of_federal_assistance_in_the_United_States)___ for ___E:non-governmental organizations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-governmental_organizations)___ (NGOs) providing ___E:abortion counseling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion_counseling)___ or referrals, advocating to decriminalize abortion, or expanding abortion services.

When in effect, the Mexico City policy is a U.S. government policy that requires foreign non-governmental organizations to certify that they will not "perform or actively promote abortion as a method of family planning" with non-U.S. funds as a condition for receiving U.S. global family planning assistance, and during its January 23, 2017 implementation any other U.S. global health assistance, including U.S. global ___E:HIV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV)___ (under ___E:PEPFAR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEPFAR)___ ) and maternal and child health (MCH) assistance.
The Mexico City policy was first implemented on January 20, 1985, by the second ___E:Reagan administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reagan_administration)___ .

Since that time, the ___E:United States Agency for International Development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Agency_for_International_Development)___ (USAID) has enforced the policy during all subsequent Republican administrations and has rescinded the policy at the direction of all Democratic administrations.

After its initial implementation by Republican President ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ in 1985,  the policy was rescinded in 1993 by Democratic President ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ ,  reinstated in 2001 by Republican President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ ,  rescinded in 2009 by Democratic President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ ,   reinstated in 2017 by Republican President ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ ,    rescinded in 2021 by Democratic President ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ ,  and reinstated in 2025 by Trump again.

Research shows that by reducing funding for family planning organizations that use abortion as one of many methods of family planning, the Mexico City policy has had the impact of increasing unintended pregnancies and abortions.

By reducing access to modern contraception and information about family planning and sexual transmitted disease, the policy has been linked to higher maternal and infant mortality rates, as well as higher incidence rates of HIV.

The policy requires non-governmental organizations to "agree as a condition of their receipt of [U.S.] federal funds" that they would "neither perform nor actively promote abortion as a method of family planning in other nations".

The policy has exceptions for abortions performed in response to ___E:rape U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rape)___ , ___E:incest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incest)___ , or life-threatening conditions.

Named for ___E:Mexico City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City)___ , the venue of the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ ___E:International Conference on Population and Development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Conference_on_Population_and_Development)___ where it was announced, the policy was instituted by ___E:U.S. President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ in 1984.    The final language of the 1984 policy was negotiated by the deputy chairman of the U.S. delegation, ___E:Alan Keyes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Keyes)___ , then an ___E:Assistant Secretary of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Assistant_Secretary_of_State)___ .

After the establishment of the Mexico City policy, organizations were required to meet its specified conditions in order to be eligible for federal funding from the United States, and as a result, several international abortion agencies no longer received a portion of their funds from this source.

The ___E:International Planned Parenthood Federation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Planned_Parenthood_Federation)___ (IPPF) did not alter its operation and lost more than 20% of its total funding.

Other ___E:family planning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_planning)___ organizations, such as the Family Guidance Association of ___E:Ethiopia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia)___ and the Planned Parenthood Association of ___E:Zambia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambia)___ , likewise did not make the changes required by the Mexico City policy and had their funding cut. NGOs in ___E:Romania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania)___ and ___E:Colombia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia)___ adapted to the new U.S. guidelines and continued to qualify for federal funding.
In 1987 and 1988, the policy was challenged by two ___E:U.S. Appeals court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_courts_of_appeals)___ rulings in DKT Memorial Fund Ltd. vs.
USAID , involving ___E:Phil Harvey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Harvey)___ and two foreign NGOs,  and Planned Parenthood Federation of America, Inc. v.
USAID .
Ultimately, the two court rulings contributed to the policy being used only against foreign NGOs, while not invoked against U.S.
NGOs.

President ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ rescinded the Mexico City policy on January 22, 1993. He referred to the policy as being ___E:"excessively broad" U:(https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/WCPD-1993-01-25/pdf/WCPD-1993-01-25-Pg88-2.pdf)___ and stated that it had "undermined efforts to promote safe and efficacious family planning programs in foreign nations".

On January 22, 2001, President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ reinstated the policy, stating, "It is my conviction that taxpayer funds should not be used to pay for abortions or advocate or actively promote abortion, either here or abroad.
It is therefore my belief that the Mexico City Policy should be restored".

In September 2007, ___E:Barbara Boxer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Boxer)___ , a ___E:Senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ from ___E:California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California)___ , created an amendment designed to lift the funding conditions put in place by the Mexico City policy.
It passed by a vote of 53–41. President Bush promised to veto any legislation which would eliminate the Mexico City policy.

The policy was rescinded again by President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ on January 23, 2009,  and further reinstated on January 23, 2017 by President ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ .

Trump not only reinstated the policy but expanded it, making it cover all global health organizations that receive U.S. government funding, rather than only family planning organizations that do, as was previously the case. This includes offices such as USAID, the Department of State, Global Aids Coordinator, Center of Disease Control and Prevention, National Institute of Health, and Department of Defense.
The nature of the policy has implications for organizations in certain countries such as ___E:South Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion_in_South_Africa)___ .
Even if these organizations support the policy itself, it is illegal for them not to inform a woman seeking an abortion of her rights, and/or refer her to a facility where she may have an abortion.

The ___E:President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President%27s_Emergency_Plan_for_AIDS_Relief)___ (PEPFAR) was excluded from the Mexico City policy under the ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ administration, but was not excluded after the Mexico City policy was reinstated on January 23, 2017.

In May 2017, ___E:Rex Tillerson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson)___ announced an expansion of the policy; originally a ban covering roughly $600 million in family planning money, the Trump policy since then applied to all international health care aid doled out by the U.S. government — nearly $9 billion.

The Mexico City policy was rescinded again by President ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ on January 28, 2021.  On January 24, 2025, President ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump)___ reinstated the Mexico City Policy.

A 2011 study that examined ___E:Sub-Saharan Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-Saharan_Africa)___ found that the Mexico City policy had the ___E:unintended consequence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unintended_consequence)___ of increasing the number of abortions, with the authors suggesting that the reduction in financial support for family planning organizations led to a greater number of accidental pregnancies.
A 2015 study of Ghana found that the policy increased unintended pregnancies and abortions.

In a 2017 editorial for The New England Journal of Medicine , Stanford University health experts Nathan Lo and Michele Barry said that research showed the policy increases unintended pregnancies and abortions.

They wrote that "the reinstatement of the Mexico City Policy is a stark example of 'evidence-free' policymaking that ignores the best scientific data, resulting in a policy that harms global health and, ultimately, the American people."  2017 editorials in The BMJ by University of Michigan Medical School health experts and The Lancet by University of Toronto, Columbia University, and ___E:Guttmacher Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guttmacher_Institute)___ health experts concluded the same.

According to a 2019 study in The Lancet , the implementation of the Mexico City policy during the ___E:George W. Bush administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush_administration)___ (2001–2009) unintentionally led to more abortions.
By limiting funding for family planning organizations, which use abortion as one of many methods of family planning, use of contraceptives reduced and pregnancies increased.
When the Mexico City policy was in effect under the Bush administration, the abortion rate was 64% higher in thirteen countries highly affected by the policy than in other comparable countries.

Under the immediately preceding ___E:Bill Clinton administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton_administration)___ when the policy was not in effect, the abortion rate in the thirteen countries was 8% lower than in the other comparable countries.
The authors of the study estimate that Bush's imposition of the Mexico City policy increased the abortion rate in the thirteen countries by 40%, and the rest of the increase had other causes.

In her 2019 book The Global Gag Rule and Women's Reproductive Health , Rutgers University economist Yana van der Meulen Rodgers commented that Mexico City policy had not reduced abortions, likely increased unsafe abortions, and adversely affected health outcomes for men, women, and children.
The policy originally enacted from 1984 to 1993 spoke to abortion only, not family planning in general.

In 2001, the policy was re-implemented and expanded to cover all voluntary family planning activities, and critics began to refer to it as the "global ___E:gag rule U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gag_rule)___ ".

These critics argue that the policy not only reduces the overall funding provided to particular NGOs, it closes off their access to ___E:USAID U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Agency_for_International_Development)___ -supplied ___E:condoms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condom)___ and other forms of ___E:contraception U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contraception)___ .

They argue this negatively impacts the ability of these NGOs to distribute birth control, leading to a downturn in contraceptive use and from there to an increase in the rates of unintended ___E:pregnancies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pregnancies)___ and abortion.
A study of nations in sub-Saharan Africa suggests that unintended pregnancies increased and abortions approximately doubled while the policy was in effect.

Critics also argue that the ban promotes restrictions on ___E:free speech U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_speech)___ , as well as restrictions on accurate medical information;    it has also been proved that the policy inhibited women worldwide from access to gynecological exams, AIDS prevention and treatment, and contraceptive options, and halted shipment of condoms and contraceptives to more than 20 countries.

The ___E:Holy See U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See)___ supports the Mexico City policy,  while the European Parliamentary Forum on Population and Development presented a petition to the ___E:United States Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ signed by 233 members condemning the policy.
The forum has stated that the policy "undermines internationally agreed consensus and goals".

Supporters of the policy have argued, using the example of the ___E:Philippines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines)___ , that the ban prevents overseas health organizations from using U.S. government funds to contravene the contraception and ___E:abortion laws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion_law#National_laws)___ of the countries in which they operate.
Supporters also argue that the policy prevents the health agencies from promoting abortion at the expense of other birth control methods.

The ___E:Sandbæk Report U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandb%C3%A6k_Report)___ of the ___E:European Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union)___ , which calls for the funding of the ___E:United Nations Population Fund U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Population_Fund)___ (UNFPA), was seen by some ___E:Catholic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Church)___ commentators as a contrast to the Mexico City policy.
The European commissioner ___E:Poul Nielson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poul_Nielson)___ said that the European Union wished to "fill the decency gap" left by the Mexico City policy.

The UNFPA states that it does not "provide support for abortion services".  ___E:Anti-abortion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-abortion)___ individuals and organizations have accused the UNFPA of supporting ___E:forced abortions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forced_abortion)___ by the ___E:Chinese government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China)___ .
The ___E:Bush administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush_administration)___ withheld funding from the agency due to concerns about its alleged involvement.
A 2002 ___E:U.S. State Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._State_Department)___ investigation found "no evidence" that UNFPA knowingly took part in forced abortions.
The organization has stated that it "has never, and will never, be involved in coercion in China or any part of the world".

In 2010, the ___E:Harper government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premiership_of_Stephen_Harper)___ in ___E:Canada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada)___ announced a maternal health development aid plan for the upcoming ___E:G8 summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/36th_G8_summit)___ which did not include financial support for abortion or contraception, drawing comparisons to the Mexico City policy.

An ___E:episode U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Boston_Legal_episodes)___ of the television series Boston Legal , "Squid Pro Quo", which originally aired on May 9, 2006, featured a case involving USAID's withdrawal of funding to an overseas non-profit organization.

An ___E:episode U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_The_West_Wing_episodes)___ of the American television series The West Wing , entitled " ___E:Privateers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_West_Wing_(season_4))___ ", featured a "gag rule" amendment of a law for overseas aid.
